chapter 01

This is not what you think

(in case you were bracing for something)

Dear Sir,

First of all — don't worry.

This is not another assignment. There is no code to debug. No output to find. No question at the end. And thankfully… no viva.

This time, Sir, you just have to sit back and read. Because there is something we wanted to tell you for a long time. We just never actually said it.

Maybe because we never knew how. Maybe because every time we thought about saying it, it felt a little awkward.

After all… you were our professor. We were your students. And that's how things normally are.

But sometimes, normal things leave behind unusual memories.

This is one of those stories.

chapter 02

Why this exists

or: the message we almost sent

We thought about sending you a normal message. Something like:

“Thank you, Sir.”

Simple. Short. Done.

But then we realised that wouldn't really explain anything. Because there isn't one particular thing we're thanking you for. It's a collection of small things.

Classes. Questions. Mistakes. Explanations. Random conversations. A few difficult days. A lot of ordinary days.

So instead of writing one short message… we decided to put the memories together.

chapter 04

Wait… you're actually like this?

the part where we started paying attention

The funny thing about people is that you can't really understand them from the first meeting.

At first, we saw the professor. Then we started seeing the teacher. And slowly, we started noticing the person.

The way you explained something when someone didn't understand. The way you didn't get irritated when the same doubt came again. The way you smiled while teaching. The way you made difficult things feel a little less difficult. The way you encouraged students instead of making them afraid of getting something wrong.

And somewhere along the way, we started thinking: “Okay… maybe Sir isn't as scary as we thought.”

chapter 05

Our class was never just about the subject

well… technically it was. but also not really.

Of course, we came to learn.

Java. Python. Programming. Logic. Concepts. Projects. Assignments.

Errors. And more errors.

Sometimes the code worked. Sometimes it absolutely refused to cooperate. Sometimes we understood the topic immediately. Sometimes we needed another explanation. Sometimes another explanation after that. And sometimes… we just sat there hoping that understanding would happen automatically.

It didn't. So you explained again.

And that's something we remember. Not because you gave one perfect explanation. But because you were willing to explain it again when we needed it. That kind of patience becomes noticeable after a while.

chapter 06

The patience we probably tested

we say “probably” because we're a little guilty

Sir, let's be honest. We definitely tested your patience.

Someone would ask a question. You would explain. Then someone else would ask the same question differently. You would explain again. Then someone would say: “Sir, one more time.” And somehow… you would explain it again.

No dramatic reaction. No making anyone feel embarrassed. Just: “Okay, let's see it again.”

At the time, we probably didn't think much about it. Now, when we look back… we realise that patience is not a small quality in a teacher. It changes how comfortable students feel while learning. Because when you know you can ask again… you aren't as afraid of being wrong. And that made our classroom experience better.

the patience meter · scientifically measured · by us
patience remaining : 100%  ·  suspicious.
chapter 07

The little things

the ones that never felt little at the time

There were many things that probably felt completely normal to you.

For you, these may have simply been parts of a normal working day. For us, they slowly became familiar parts of college life.

And that's how memories usually happen. Not through one huge event. But through hundreds of small moments that don't seem important until you look back.

chapter 08

When things didn't go perfectly

and the class still happened anyway

Not every class had perfect conditions. Sometimes equipment wasn't available. Sometimes things didn't work. Sometimes the situation wasn't ideal.

But somehow, the class still continued. You still came. You still taught. You still tried to make sure we got something out of the class.

Maybe you saw that as simply doing your job. And technically… yes. It was your job. But doing a job and putting genuine effort into it are two different things.

We noticed that difference.

We may not have said anything at the time. But we noticed.

WE NOTICED.

chapter 10

The days we needed encouragement

every student has those days. these were some of ours.

Some days you feel confident. Some days you understand everything. And some days you look at a problem and think: “Why did I choose this?”

Sometimes we doubted ourselves. Sometimes we thought something was too difficult. Sometimes we simply needed someone to say: “Try again.”

And your encouragement often came at exactly those moments.

You probably don't remember every conversation. You probably don't remember every sentence. But students don't always remember the exact words. Sometimes they remember what they did after hearing them.

They tried again.

chapter 11

Somewhere along the way

this is probably the hardest part to explain

Because nothing dramatic happened. There wasn't one particular day when we decided: “Okay, Sir is now important to us.”

It happened slowly. Class after class. Conversation after conversation. Question after question. Small moment after small moment.

You started as our professor.
chapter 12

And here is the funny part

you probably have no idea. that is the funny part.

You were simply doing what you normally do. Teaching. Explaining. Correcting. Encouraging. Smiling. Moving on to the next topic.

Meanwhile, somewhere in the classroom… four students were quietly collecting memories.

meanwhile, in sir's class…

You: teaching like it's a normal Tuesday.

You: patient, smiling, moving on to the next topic.

Us: quietly memorising all of it for no reason at all.

AND YOU DIDN'T EVEN KNOW.

(tap the memo. the stamp is the best part.)

We never walked up to you and said: “Sir, just so you know, this class is going to become a memory for us.”

Obviously not. We had assignments to finish. We had classes to attend. We had exams to survive.

So we kept everything to ourselves.

chapter 13

Why didn't we say anything?

we rehearsed it. once. in our heads. it did not go well.

Maybe because saying these things directly feels awkward. Imagine us suddenly standing in front of you and saying…

the conversation we never had
“Sir, we really appreciate your patience.”us · imagined · day 1
“Sir, you motivate us.”us · imagined · day 2
“Sir, you are one of our favourite teachers.”us · imagined · day 3

It sounds nice. But saying it out loud? Very difficult. So we did what students usually do. We said nothing. We attended class. We listened. We laughed. We asked questions. We went home. And thought: “Maybe we'll tell Sir someday.”

Then another day came. And another. And suddenly… we're making this website instead.

chapter 15

If you don't remember us…

that's okay. this part is important anyway.

Maybe after some time, you'll teach another batch. Then another. And another. You'll meet hundreds of students. You'll probably remember some clearly. Some vaguely. And some… maybe not at all.

And that's completely understandable. We aren't making this because we expect you to remember our names forever. We aren't asking for anything.

We simply wanted to leave one message with you.

Even if we were ordinary students in your classroom… your classes weren't ordinary to us.
chapter 16

One day, college will end

which sounds impossible. it isn't. we checked the calendar.

Right now, college feels like something that's always going to be there. The classrooms. The corridors. The timetable. The same people. The same routine.

But eventually it ends. We'll leave. We'll start working. We'll build careers. We'll move to different places. We'll meet new people. We'll have new responsibilities. We'll get busy. And life will continue. We won't be students forever.

chapter 19

The letter

the one we kept in our drafts. both of them.

♥
Dear Sir,

Your way of teaching, your patience, your guidance, and the way you always encourage us have made a beautiful impact on us.

There may come a day when we leave this college, move on to our careers, and get busy with our lives. There may be new classrooms, new teachers, new workplaces, and completely different lives ahead of us.

But when we look back at this part of our journey, there will always be certain teachers we remember more clearly.

Teachers who didn't simply teach a subject. Teachers who made learning feel easier. Teachers who gave students confidence when they needed it. Teachers who were patient when students were still figuring things out.

You will always be one of those teachers for us.

Thank you for believing in us even when we doubted ourselves. Thank you for guiding us when we were confused. Thank you for teaching us. Thank you for motivating us. Thank you for being someone we could always look up to.

And most importantly… thank you for being you.

— with gratitude, from your students (the four who never said it)
Some teachers are remembered for what they taught. But the best teachers are remembered for how they made their students feel.

And the people behind this little surprise are…

Your Students.

Okay, Sir. Now you know. It was us.

The same four students who sat in your classes. The same four students who asked questions. The same four students who sometimes understood immediately… and sometimes definitely did not. The same four students who never actually told you all of this. Until now.

We don't know what you thought about us as students. Maybe we were just another group in another class. And that's okay. We never needed to be anything more than that.

We simply wanted you to know that your teaching reached us in ways you probably didn't see.

Thank you, Sir. For the classes. For the patience. For the explanations.
For the encouragement. For the laughs.
For the difficult days. For the ordinary days.
And for being part of this chapter of our lives.

We came into your classroom to learn a subject.

We are leaving with much more than that.

Some teachers are remembered for what they taught. But the best teachers are remembered for how they made their students feel.

And Sir… we're glad we finally told you.
